title: Scan into a buffer without a width (c)
description: The code reads formatted input with fscanf and a plain string conversion. Those conversions carry no width, so any input longer than the destination overflows it. This lexical rule flags the scan; the reviewer adds widths or switches parser.
remediation: Give every string conversion a width tied to the destination, or read a bounded line and parse it, for example fgets into a bounded buffer, then parse.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the scan call without inspecting the format string.
